newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index up, market still depressed.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index up, market still depressed.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index rose marginally on Friday but the market was on average still depressed, brokers and floor dealers said.
The index gained 13.11 points to stand at 3042.74. Turnover was at 10.584 million shillings traded on 362,901 shares from 7.459 million shillings from 200,988 shares Thursday.
Local investors bought a lot of 146,000 shares of Credit Finance Bank at 19 on the special board, accounting for about a third of the total shares traded on Friday.
Brokers said the market remained depressed with very little interest from investors, especially institutional investors.
"Institutional investors, in particular insurance firms are not keen on investing in the market because of the high tax levied on income from their investments," a senior broker said.
The tax is currently pegged at 35 percent.
"Investors' savings have also been depleted by the recent (primary) issues in the bourse," the broker added.
Foreign investors bought 4,916 shares of Kenya Breweries at 48, some 4,082 shares of Kenya Power & Lighting Co at 117, and 12,612 shares of the same at 120.

Kenya Power & Lighting Co is Kenya's sole distributor of power. "For as long as it enjoys a monopoly, its shares will continue doing well. Given that the government has listed the institution for privatisation, investors anticipate an increase in share price," one broker said.
Rea Vipingo traded 14,350 shares at 10.20 from 10.15 while Kenya Airways traded 69,972 shares at 9.50 from 9.55.
